text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT P1: Cross-region routing anomaly detected for /v1/generate across eu-west-1 -> us-west-2 paths. Increased 5xx and tail latency starting 10:24 UTC. Pager issued to @samir (oncall).

samir (oncall): acked. I'm on it. seeing 95p latency spike from eu clients hitting us-west endpoints, lots of 502/504s. any recent routing changes? :thinking_face:

kevin (netops): I deployed a weight tweak to the latency-based policy at 09:56 UTC to shift some spillover away from eu-west-1 (trying to drain a degraded AZ). It should have been a gradual weight but I accidentally set override precedence higher than pinning. rolling back now if that's likely.

lia (platform): adding visibility: traces show requests that should pin to eu-west-1 are being routed to us-west-2. healthchecks for eu-west-1 look fine from inside the region, but external perf probes show packet loss from certain POPs. Could be stale DNS or a policy precedence bug.

samir (oncall): can you dump the active routing policy and recent commits? Also need DNS answers from a few edge locations (dig + curl).

kevin (netops): running now:

```
$ redwoodctl routing policy get --name=global-latency-fallback
commit: c4d9f2b
deployed_by: kevin
deployed_at: 2026-03-15T09:56:12Z
rules:
  - precedence: 100
    match: latency < 120ms
    action: prefer_local
  - precedence: 200
    match: region_pin == true
    action: pin_region
```

kevin (netops): aha — precedence ordering is wrong (latency rule has higher precedence than pin). That would override explicit pins. I pushed a quick rollback to previous commit id b7a1e3, reverting precedence. rolling back now: `redwoodctl routing policy rollback --commit=b7a1e3` :construction:

ops-runner-bot: rollback started for policy global-latency-fallback by kevin at 2026-03-15T10:01:03Z

samir (oncall): good. while that's in progress, maria — any customer escalations? Are specific customers impacted? we need ETA for mitigation.

maria (support): we've got 12 active tickets and one enterprise customer (acorn.tech) reported degraded throughput and failing requests. CS notified them and opened an interim status update. They want estimated time to fix.

lia (platform): rollback applied at 10:02:14Z. policy state now shows commit=b7a1e3 active. However, I'm still seeing cross-region traffic for a subset of POPs — suggests caching (DNS or edge policy cache) is holding older routing decisions. TTLs on our global CNAME were set to 300s normally but last week's change increased it to 3600s in one of the providers. that could explain slow convergence.

samir (oncall): can we force purge or reduce TTLs at DNS provider and edge? list provider and record IDs.

kevin (netops): provider=fastedge-dns, record id=Z_abc123. Current TTL=3600. I'll stage TTL=60 and request immediate refresh.

```
$ fastedge-cli dns update --record Z_abc123 --ttl 60
> response: accepted, async-refresh queued
```

kevin (netops): also asked edge to purge POP caches for route decisions: `fastedge-cli pop purge --tag=eu-pop-* --route-cache` — started.

ops-runner-bot: dns ttl change accepted, purge job queued (job id purge-9921).

samir (oncall): monitoring metrics. Are we seeing 5xx drop? any errors changing?

lia (platform): partial improvement: eu-middle POPs reverted to eu-west-1 routing after ~45s, but some fringe POPs still sending to us-west-2. Dig response from a problematic POP:

```
$ dig +short @203.0.113.45 api.redwood.example.com
52.23.11.9  # us-west-2
```

samir (oncall): that POP IP is cached. we need fallback mitigation: add a temporary header-based override so that clients with X-Region: EU get forced to eu endpoints. Can we do that at the API gateway?

lia (platform): yes, we can add a quick header rule at the gateway layer and set it for 10 minutes while caches expire. deploying rule now:

```
$ gatewayctl route update --name=force-region-from-header --match 'header:X-Region=EU' --set 'target_region=eu-west-1' --ttl 600
> applied
```

samir (oncall): applied. pushing a targeted rate-limit increase to eu-west-1 to handle now-concentrated traffic.

kevin (netops): also requested the DNS provider to run a force-refresh on their authoritative edge: `fastedge-cli dns refresh --record Z_abc123 --force` (they confirmed). propagation should finish within 120s.

maria (support): letting customers know we've applied a rollback and temporary gateway rule; purges and TTL drop are in flight. estimated time to full recovery 5-10 minutes. customers are appreciative of the quick update.

samir (oncall): monitoring — good signal: 5xx count trending down, tail latency improving. still watching for any new anomalies. we should open a full post-incident follow-up: root cause seems to be a bad precedence change plus long DNS TTL on one provider leading to stale routing decisions.

kevin (netops): agreed. I'll open PR to add a pre-deploy check that validates policy precedence invariants (pin rules must have higher precedence than latency fallback). Also add an automated TTL sanity check on DNS changes. assigning to self for the follow-up.

lia (platform): we should also add a smoke-test that probes multiple POPs for pin correctness during deploys (simulate pinned client headers). I'll file a ticket.

ops-runner-bot: incident transitioned to "mitigated" at 2026-03-15T10:09:21Z by samir (oncall)

samir (oncall): handing off to kevin for postmortem and to lia for monitoring improvements. remaining action items: kevin - policy predeploy check + DNS TTL guard; lia - POP smoke tests and gateway rule automation; maria - customer follow-ups and status close. I'll close the pager after one hour of stable metrics.

maria (support): will send update to affected customers and close the support tickets once we verify stability.

kevin (netops): filing incident postmortem now. preliminary RCA: accidental precedence change in routing policy + provider-side TTL set to 3600s caused linger. Mitigation steps successful: policy rollback, TTL reduction, edge purge, temporary gateway header rule.

samir (oncall): thanks everyone. leaving thread open for a few more checks. :white_check_mark:

ops-runner-bot: thread auto-close scheduled in 3 days unless flagged.
